div.div: سَأْبٌ and ↓ مِسْأَبٌ A [skin such as is termed] زِقّ, (S, M, K,) for wine: (M:) or such as is large: (M, K:) or a زِقّ of any kind: (M:) or a receptacle of skin, or leather, in which the زِقّ is put: (M, K:) the former also occurs in a verse in which it is read without ء, for the sake of the rhyme: (M:) and its pl. is سُؤُوبٌ: (S, M, K:) and (so in the S, but in the K “ or, ”) the latter (مسأب) signifies a skin for honey; (S, K;) and in a verse of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, (S, M, K,) cited voce خَافَةٌ, (S, M,) it is written مِسَابٌ, (S, M, K,) without ء: (S, M:) and it signifies also a skin in which clarified butter is put. (S and L voce مِسَادٌ.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
